rows.why: S1 asks how case and padding are cleaned before matching, which is item 4's question. Item 4 trims and lowercases, so "Draft", " PUBLISHED " and "Merged" read as draft, published and merged.

Item 3 asks which old spellings map to which status. Its pick maps only 'in review' and explicitly rejects 'done'. So 'under review' (from "under_review") and 'live' (from "LIVE") would read as null, not review and published.

Item 2 asks what reading does with a value that matches no status or old spelling. Its pick returns null instead of guessing the nearest status, which is what S3 expects. Item 6 also returns null for empty or space-only values, so it agrees too.
No item asks whether a valid status is stored unchanged. Item 1 is about near-miss spellings, and either answer to it would still store "review" as "review".

Item 1 asks whether writing normalises near-miss spellings or rejects them. Its pick throws for anything other than the exact lowercase values, including 'in-review' and ' draft', so old spellings are never accepted on write. Item 8's message also includes the value as given.

Item 10 asks how unreadable values are reported in a batch read. Its pick reports the raw stored strings, deduplicated by exact string and sorted, which matches 'each distinct original value once, sorted, exactly as it was stored'.
